rationale: Lens: contract stability of the additive DerivationFailed/DerivationError fields. Full consumer enumeration of Context.Phase at 68ede240 (non-test): cmd/mindspec/instruct_tail.go emitInstruct (consults DerivationFailed — honest), internal/instruct/run.go arrival point 1 at line 121-135 (consults — honest), internal/instruct/run.go arrival point 2 at line 157 (reads only BeadID for enrichment; mode already came from ResolveModeWithCache which errors on genuine failure — safe), internal/resolve/target.go:125 (reads only SpecID, which is path-derived and honest — safe), internal/guard/guard.go:52 (reads SpecID/EpicID/BeadID, never Phase; ambient never-block per ADR-0042 — safe), internal/hook/hook.go:211 (reads Phase into HookState.Mode without consulting DerivationFailed — enforcement outcome unchanged in every branch combination I traced, finding only), and internal/cleanup/cleanup.go:49 (reads Phase as the guard on a DESTRUCTIVE operation — affected, see the blocking finding). The blocking problem: the disclosure and the DerivationFailed doc comment (derive.go:115-127) claim Phase's historical fallback VALUES are unchanged for existing callers, but the WorktreeSpec branch gates its ModeSpec backfill on `!ctx.DerivationFailed` (derive.go:660), so on a genuine bd/Dolt failure in a spec worktree Phase changed from "spec" (pre-bead-5, verified against 68ede240^) to "". The WorktreeBead branch, by contrast, correctly preserves its ModeImplement fallback value while setting the flag, and WorktreeMain was "" on error both before and after — the field is genuinely additive in two of three branches and un-additive in the third. The concrete casualty is cleanup.Run's active-spec refusal (cleanup.go:50: `ctx.Phase != ModeIdle && ctx.Phase != ""`): run `mindspec cleanup <spec>` from inside the spec worktree while bd is down and the guard that previously refused ("spec X is still active") now passes, letting exec.Cleanup remove the worktree and delete the branch. A fail-closed destructive-path guard became fail-open, silently, under an "additive, values unchanged" disclosure. The fix is one line and fully compatible with the bead's honesty goals, since both honest consumers check DerivationFailed BEFORE Phase. Everything else under my lens held: the R1.4 split is intact (ResolveModeWithCache still errors so state show refuses; emitInstruct/renderIndeterminateTail and run.go's handleIndeterminate return errors only on render failure, so the indeterminate form never fails the verb); AC-4's two completeTail branches are mutually exclusive (FormatResult returns early on NextModeIndeterminate; complete.go's tail branches on the same flag, never a re-derivation); and step-6.5's skip-on-indeterminate composes safely with bead 6 — the contracted M/R/S/G/T staged machinery occupies Run steps 2.5-5 (pre-panel sequence, snapshot, materialization, merge), all of which complete before step 6's advanceState, so bead 6 needs no reshape of the completeFetchChildrenFn seam; it must merely count bead-5's new early return (complete.go:1382-1392) as a completion path when placing its terminal marker clear (advisory forwarded as a finding). Tests: internal/phase, internal/instruct, internal/complete, internal/cleanup, internal/hook all pass in the bead worktree; cmd/mindspec's initial failures were my environment's globally-installed mindspec pre-commit hook firing inside test fixtures (blocked `git commit` on fixture main), not the bead — targeted re-runs with MINDSPEC_ALLOW_MAIN=1 pass, matching disclosure. The pin-inventory claim is R2's lens; I did not duplicate it.
concrete_changes_required: internal/phase/derive.go:660 — restore the WorktreeSpec branch's unconditional ModeSpec backfill (drop `&& !ctx.DerivationFailed`), making DerivationFailed genuinely additive exactly as the WorktreeBead branch already does with its preserved ModeImplement fallback and as the field's own doc comment (derive.go:115-127) and the commit disclosure claim. Both honest consumers (cmd/mindspec/instruct_tail.go:30 and internal/instruct/run.go:125) check DerivationFailed before Phase, so the indeterminate rendering is unaffected; the restored value re-closes internal/cleanup/cleanup.go:50's active-spec refusal, which this gate silently flipped from fail-closed to fail-open for a bd outage in a spec worktree (destructive path: worktree removal + branch deletion). Alternative if the "" value is deliberately wanted: make cleanup.Run consult DerivationFailed and refuse with the real reason — but that grows scope into an undeclared file, so the one-line revert is preferred. Either way, add at least one internal/phase unit test pinning a DerivationFailed case at the derive level (grep shows ZERO direct test references to DerivationFailed anywhere — all five setting sites are covered only transitively through internal/instruct and cmd tests).

findings.title: WorktreeSpec Phase fallback value changed under an 'additive, values unchanged' disclosure; cleanup's destructive-path guard fails open
findings.detail: derive.go:660 gates the ModeSpec backfill on !ctx.DerivationFailed, so a genuine bd/Dolt failure in a spec worktree now yields Phase="" where pre-bead-5 code (verified at 68ede240^) yielded "spec". internal/cleanup/cleanup.go:49-52 guards worktree removal + branch deletion on Phase being a non-idle, non-empty value and does not consult DerivationFailed: the refusal that previously fired for this window now passes. This contradicts the DerivationFailed doc comment's own contract statement and the commit message's 'Phase's historical fallback VALUES are unchanged for existing callers'. The WorktreeBead branch shows the intended design (fallback value preserved, flag additive). See concrete_changes_required for the one-line fix.

findings.title: hook.ReadState copies Phase into HookState.Mode without consulting DerivationFailed — outcome-unchanged, message-level only
findings.detail: internal/hook/hook.go:213 sets hs.Mode = ctx.Phase. Traced against internal/hook/dispatch.go: the protected-branch block fires in ANY mode (message may read 'mode: idle' during a genuine bd outage — a fabricated mode claim in user-visible hook output, but pre-existing for the main-checkout case and never altering the Block/Pass outcome); the spec/-branch implement-mode check failed open identically before and after this bead (fabricated 'spec' != 'implement' then, '' now — both Pass). Never-block ambient consumer per ADR-0042, so internal-safe by this panel's standard. Worth a future-bead note: spec 128's honesty mandate arguably extends to displaying 'indeterminate' in the protected-branch block message when DerivationFailed.

findings.title: Bead-6 forward-compat: the AC-4b early return is a third completion path for the terminal marker clear
findings.detail: complete.go:1382-1392's indeterminate return exits Run after all terminal mutations (close at step 4, merge/worktree-removal at step 5) but before step 6.5. Bead 6's contracted S-stage machinery (plan §Bead 6 step 4: M/R/S/G/T, snapshot, materialization, merge) occupies steps 2.5-5 and therefore completes before this return — bead 5's seam needs NO reshape. But the plan's 'terminal marker clear on both completion paths' must be read as 'all Run exits after the merge': if bead 6 places its clear at the end of Run instead of at step 5's conclusion, the indeterminate return would strand a stale stage marker. Recommend the orchestrator carry this note into bead 6's staged prompt.

findings.title: R1.4 split verified held; residual routing to beads 4/5 verified discharged
findings.detail: state show's refusal is untouched (resolve.ResolveModeWithCache still returns a real error on genuine failure; no state-show file in the diff), and the instruct-side indeterminate form never fails its verb (emitInstruct/renderIndeterminateTail and run.go's handleIndeterminate return errors only for render failures). Both instruct arrival points in run.go consult DerivationFailed. Separately, completeSyncPhase's recorded residual ('routed to beads 4/5') is discharged: bead 4's agreement_table_test.go:604 names completeSyncPhase's write shape explicitly, and bead 5's ModePlan rewording covers the result-message half.

findings.title: Zero direct unit pins on DerivationFailed at the derive level
findings.detail: grep over all *_test.go finds no reference to DerivationFailed: the five setting sites in ResolveContextFromDirWithCache (bead-worktree lineage failure, bead-worktree phase failure, spec-worktree phase failure, spec-worktree AllEpics probe, main-worktree discovery failure) are exercised only transitively via internal/instruct and cmd/mindspec tests, which pass through just two of the five. The beadsDirMissing guard likewise has no derive-level pin (it is exercised via the three internal/instruct fixtures the disclosure names). Folded into the concrete change: one derive-level table test over the five sites would pin the additive contract itself, not just its downstream rendering.
